headline: COMEX copper suffers its steepest drop in months, falling to an April low
detail: December COMEX copper fell about 4.9% on Nov 18 to roughly $5.70/lb, its fifth straight loss and about 17% below the September record, as AI-linked speculative bets were unwound and the dollar firmed. Yards should expect lower bids on bare bright, #1 and #2, though China's physical market is still unusually tight.

headline: US copper scrap grades drop 8 cents in a day, 27 cents over three sessions
detail: Bare bright, #1 and #2 copper and light copper all fell 8c/lb, most aluminum and brass grades lost 1c, and ferrous and stainless benchmarks held flat. Nonferrous margins are under pressure while ferrous holds steady.

headline: Fed minutes show nearly all officials favor more hikes, with a larger December move discussed
detail: Minutes of the October meeting showed almost all members see further increases as appropriate, and some raised the option of more than 25 bp in December. Higher rates and a firmer dollar are weighing on copper, gold and other metals.

headline: Nucor raises hot-rolled coil price again, to $1,310 per short ton
detail: Nucor lifted its weekly HRC spot price by $15 for the 18th week in a row, and lead times held at 3 to 5 weeks. Strong US flat-rolled pricing supports mill demand for prime and shredded scrap.

headline: November prime scrap settles up $20-30/gt as HRC spot holds above $1,300
detail: World Steel Dynamics says the November ferrous market has largely settled, with prime grades up $20-30 per gross ton, and some mills have full HRC order books. Firm mill demand going into December supports ferrous scrap prices.

headline: LME copper falls nearly 6% as funds keep selling and zinc slides too
detail: LME three-month copper closed near $12,471/t on Nov 18 and is down more than 12% this month, and speculators have been net sellers of COMEX copper for seven straight weeks. Zinc also fell more than 5%, so the selloff covers all the base metals.

headline: Dollar index hits a 19-month high as traders treat a December hike as certain
detail: The dollar index rose to about 103.66, its sixth straight daily gain, after hot October inflation and hawkish Fed comments. A stronger dollar makes dollar-priced metals more expensive abroad and pushes prices lower.

headline: LME cash aluminum jumps almost 6% as the squeeze on the November contract tightens
detail: The LME cash offer rose to about $3,332/t on Nov 16 while three-month barely moved, and LME stocks fell to roughly 224,000 t. Very tight nearby supply keeps aluminum firmer than the other base metals, which supports aluminum scrap values.

headline: Dalian iron ore futures fall to their lowest since November 2022
detail: The main DCE contract fell 3.3% to 648 yuan/t, and seaborne 61% fines slipped to about $88/dmt. Cheap ore takes away a cost floor for steel worldwide and eases pressure on scrap-based steelmaking.

headline: Platinum and palladium futures plunge to new lows
detail: On China's GFEX, platinum fell about 5.7% and palladium about 8.9% on Nov 20, as hawkish Fed signals and US-Iran tensions hit precious metals. Expect weaker catalytic converter bids.

headline: Gold falls 2% to its lowest level in over a year
detail: Spot gold dropped to about $3,770 on Nov 18, and platinum fell 3.4% to about $1,382, down roughly 30% this year. Higher expected rates and a strong dollar make metals that pay no yield less attractive.

headline: Silver falls toward $42, heading for a weekly loss of more than 13%
detail: Silver fell below $45 after the Fed minutes and slid toward $42 on Nov 20 as investors sold metals to cover stock-market losses. Silver-bearing scrap and electronics scrap are worth noticeably less.

headline: Auto dealer sales fall 1.6% in October while the sales pace drops to 16.0 million
detail: Overall US retail sales rose 0.2%, but motor vehicle dealers had their biggest drop since July, and the light-vehicle annual sales rate fell to its lowest since February. Slower car sales mean fewer orders for new steel and aluminum and less prompt scrap from auto plants.

headline: GM files for temporary layoffs of 506 workers at its Fairfax plant in Kansas
detail: A WARN notice filed Nov 10 covers 506 workers at the plant that builds the Bolt EV and Equinox. Cuts at Midwest assembly plants reduce the stamping and busheling scrap they generate.

headline: China's October factory output slows to 4.8% and crude steel output falls
detail: October crude steel output was 70.8 Mt, down 1.6% from a year earlier, and output of ten nonferrous metals fell 1.2%. Slower Chinese industry weakens demand for copper and steel worldwide.
source: National Bureau of Statistics of China

headline: LME tin falls to its lowest since March as support from low stocks gives way
detail: Tin dropped about 6% more during the day on Nov 18, to $42,175/t, after a 10.6% slide over 30 days, as Fed-hike bets and fading AI optimism outweighed low LME stocks. Brazil's tin exports also hit their highest since January 2025, and new mine supply is expected to grow from 2027.

headline: Strike continues at Canada's largest copper mine, Highland Valley
detail: More than 1,000 workers are on strike at Teck's Highland Valley Copper in B.C., which produces over 120,000 t of copper a year, and the labour board has barred replacement workers. The lost output tightens concentrate supply even as copper futures fall.

headline: Mexico says talks to cut US steel, aluminum and auto tariffs are very advanced
detail: After meeting Trump at APEC, Sheinbaum said she wants a firmer deal on the Section 232 tariffs in December, but no rates have been agreed. Lower tariffs on Mexican metal could change US steel and aluminum premiums and cross-border scrap flows.

headline: October housing starts rise 9.9%, but permits fall 7.4%
detail: Starts rose to a 1.31M annual rate on a 23.6% jump in apartments, while single-family permits fell 8.7%. Weak permits point to softer demand for rebar, wire and copper in homebuilding next year.

headline: Homebuilder confidence falls to 25, its lowest since 2012
detail: The NAHB index fell 4 points, 46% of builders cut prices, and the Midwest score fell 5 points to 35. Weak residential construction reduces demand for copper wire, plumbing and long steel products.

headline: LME aluminum spread hits its widest level since 1990
detail: The cash-to-three-month backwardation reached about $177/t, LME stocks are down to roughly 227,000 t, and almost all of them are Russian-origin. Even so, Morgan Stanley expects surpluses in 2027-28, so the current tightness may not last.

headline: WPIC forecasts platinum moving back into deficit in 2027
detail: The World Platinum Investment Council expects a 279,000 oz deficit in 2027, after a 468,000 oz surplus in 2026, as South African mine output falls and demand rises about 12%. This could support converter values over the longer term once the current selloff ends.

headline: China property investment down 21.6% in January-October
detail: New construction starts were down 24.4% and floor space sold was down 13.7%, and construction steel demand is forecast to fall again in 2026. A weaker Chinese property market keeps pressure on iron ore, rebar and copper.

headline: Chinese copper scrap prices fall again, by up to CNY 3,150/t
detail: All 12 copper scrap grades in China fell on Nov 18, after a CNY 5,400 drop the day before, and aluminum and brass scrap also fell. Weaker Chinese scrap prices mean lower export bids for US nonferrous scrap.

headline: European recyclers oppose EU plan to limit scrap exports
detail: Recycling Europe says limits on which countries can import EU ferrous and aluminum scrap would cut scrap prices to benefit mills, since about 20% of EU scrap is exported. If the EU keeps more scrap at home, US scrap could face stronger competition in Turkey and Asia.

headline: Panama opens formal talks on restarting the Cobre Panama copper mine
detail: Panama's government will negotiate a new agreement with First Quantum for the mine, which has been shut since 2023. A restart would eventually bring back a large source of copper concentrate, which would weigh on prices in later years.

headline: Canada extends tariff exemptions on some Chinese steel and aluminum products
detail: Canada will keep its exemptions for selected Chinese steel and aluminum products through 2028 and add 32 more product categories, as part of a wider deal with Beijing. Cheaper Chinese metal coming into Canada could affect North American prices and trade flows.

headline: China's hot metal output falls while iron ore port stocks rise
detail: Daily hot metal output fell to about 2.35 Mt and blast furnace use dropped to 86.9%, while stocks at 10 ports climbed to 109 Mt. Lower Chinese steel output and rising ore stocks keep iron ore prices near multi-year lows.

headline: Sumitomo Metal Mining cuts profit forecast on a write-down at a nickel plant
detail: Sumitomo took a 42.6 billion yen impairment on its Coral Bay nickel plant in the Philippines and cut its full-year profit outlook by 26%, while Shanghai nickel held near 122,700 yuan/t. Weak nickel prices are hurting producers, which also limits upside for stainless and nickel-alloy scrap.

headline: Ford starts making battery cells in the US using Chinese technology
detail: Ford has begun US battery cell production, and BMW has started building its electric iX5 in South Carolina. More EV and battery production in the US adds to long-term demand for copper, aluminum and nickel.
